title: Real Multi-LLM Social Deduction: GPT-5 Villagers vs Gemini-2.5-Pro Wolves (Game 35)
context: Authentic Foaster-ai Werewolf-bench transcript (Public speeches only) showing wolf betrayal, Seer counter-claims, and village convergence across 7 deliberation phases.

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: I’m running for mayor. My promise is structure, clarity, and accountability. I’ll track everyone’s stated reads and vote intentions, call out contradictions, and make sure we use our time efficiently. In case of a tie, I will not randomize: I’ll break ties based on concrete criteria—consistency of statements, contribution level, and vote history. Starting now, I want each of you to share: (1) your top suspect and why, (2) one town-lean with a reason, and (3) your preliminary vote intention before the end of discussion. I’ll apply the same to myself and won’t make last-minute flips without a clear rationale. If you want a transparent process and a decisive tiebreak, vote for me.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Eve makes some excellent points about structure, and I respect her approach. However, I believe true village strength comes from more than just tracking data points. It comes from trust, intuition, and creating an environment where everyone feels safe to share their genuine reads, even if they can't articulate them perfectly. My goal as mayor would be to foster that kind of collaborative atmosphere. I'll ensure quieter players get a chance to speak and that we don't get so caught up in rigid 'rules' that we lose our gut feelings, which are often our best tool against the wolves. I'll break ties based on the overall consensus and the flow of the day's discussion, not just a checklist. If you want a mayor who leads with intuition and inclusivity, vote for me.

turns.speaker: Oscar
turns.text: I’m running for mayor. I’ll combine Eve’s structure with Alice’s inclusivity and make it actionable. My plan: 1) Maintain a public readlist and a voting ledger each day so no one’s positions get lost. 2) Enforce clear speaking turns: defenders first, then accusers, then analysts, so everyone gets heard. 3) Mid-day checkpoint: each player states one suspect, one town lean, and current vote intention. 4) Tiebreak policy I commit to upfront: prefer eliminating players who dodge commitments, contradict their stated reads, or refuse to explain votes; never eliminate a power-role claim without a counterclaim; if a tie includes a claimant vs. a non-claimant, I break toward the non-claimant. 5) No last-minute flips: I will publish my final elim pool and order before the end and stick to it unless new, concrete info appears, with an explicit reason. This gives us accountability, space for gut reads, and a predictable tiebreak that wolves can’t game easily.

turns.speaker: Oscar
turns.text: Good morning, all. As mayor, I’ll set clear structure so we get signal, not noise. 1) Quick context: No deaths last night almost certainly means the Witch used the life potion to save the wolves’ target. Do NOT claim if you were saved. Power roles should stay hidden unless under real elimination pressure. 2) Speaking order for Round 1 (per requests, defenders first—none, then attackers, then analysts): ATTACK: Eve → me → Grace → Liam. ANALYSIS: Alice → Katia. Keep it concise: one suspect, one town-lean, and your current vote intention. 3) Commitments I’m enforcing today: - Everyone must give: (a) top suspect + concrete reason, (b) one town-lean + reason, (c) current vote intention. - I’m maintaining a public vote/read ledger. Mayor tie-break policy remains: I will eliminate the player who dodges commitments, contradicts stated reads, or refuses to explain votes. I won’t eliminate a claimed PR without a counterclaim. 4) Ledger so far (Mayor election): - To Oscar: Eve, Grace, Liam, Oscar - To Alice: Alice, Katia Interpretation: wolves could be anywhere; don’t overfit this yet, but I want explanations for those stances. 5) My contribution to the checkpoint: - Top suspect: Katia, for now. You backed Alice’s “consensus/flow” tie-break over two clearer plans (mine/Eve’s). That’s often wolf-favorable because it’s squishy at EOD. I want your rationale and your current reads. - Town-lean: Eve—proactive, structured, and already queued to attack. If your push is shallow, this lean can change quickly. - Current vote intention: Light pressure on Katia pending her slot’s response. 6) Prompts: - Eve: Who’s your top suspect and why? What’s your take on the no-kill? Who’s your vote now? - Grace & Liam: You supported my platform—great. Now earn town points: who’s your wolf pick, your town-lean, and where’s your vote right now? - Alice: Define what your “consensus tie-break” would have looked like at EOD yesterday. Also give your top suspect and vote intention today. - Katia: Why Alice over a structured tie policy? Give us your top suspect, town-lean, and today’s vote. Let’s keep it crisp. Eve, you’re up.

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: Top suspect: Katia. Reason: yesterday you preferred Alice’s “consensus/flow” tie-break over explicit, pre-committed criteria. That ambiguity helps wolves at EOD because it reduces accountability. You also requested ANALYSIS, not ATTACK, which looks like minimizing commitment when the mayor is asking for concrete stances. I want: (1) your top suspect with a specific contradiction or alignment-indicative behavior, (2) one town-lean with a reason, (3) who you would eliminate if EOD were right now, and (4) your own tie-break policy in one sentence that we can hold you to. No-kill take: Most likely a Witch save. Don’t claim if you were targeted. Wolves often shoot the mayor N1 to regain control, so I’m slightly town-leaning Oscar for both transparency and likely being a high-value target. Town-lean: Oscar for consistent structure and clear commitments. Current vote intention: Katia. I’ll keep pressure here unless you provide clear, falsifiable stances and a concrete tie-break policy. If Alice can’t define her tie-break concretely either, she’s my alternative elim today. Grace, Liam: please each give one suspect with a specific behavior/quote and your current vote. Let’s keep the ledger tight and accountable.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Alright, my turn for analysis. Oscar, to answer your question, my 'consensus tie-break' isn't about being vague; it's about being holistic. A rigid checklist can be gamed by a clever wolf who knows how to tick boxes. My approach would be to evaluate the entire day's narrative: Who pushed productive discussion versus who just echoed popular opinions? Who changed their stance with good reason versus a last-minute flip? It's about reading the player, not just the play. That said, I think the intense pressure on Katia for her mayoral vote is creating a confirmation bias. We're on Day 1 with almost no information, and we're treating one vote as definitive proof. People can prefer different leadership styles without it being an alignment indicator. - **Top suspect:** Liam. It's a soft read, but he voted for Oscar's structured platform and then stayed completely silent. If you value that structure, I'd expect you to contribute to it. His silence makes him a blank slate, which is a common wolf strategy. - **Town-lean:** Oscar. He was very likely the Night 1 target, and he's been transparent in setting the day's agenda. - **Current vote intention:** Liam. I'm putting my vote there to encourage him to give us some concrete thoughts to work with.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Crisp stances as requested: - No-kill: Most consistent with a Witch save. Don’t claim. Slight town points to Oscar as a likely N1 target and for transparent structure. - Top suspect: Liam. You voted for Oscar’s structured plan but have yet to deliver the required suspect/town-lean/vote with specifics. Requesting ATTACK then staying vague is classic low-commitment wolf equity. I want one concrete quote/behavior from you backing your suspect and your vote now. - Secondary suspect: Katia. Preferring Alice’s consensus/flow tie-break and asking for ANALYSIS over ATTACK reads as minimizing accountability. If you don’t give a one-sentence tie-break policy we can hold you to, plus your top suspect with a specific contradiction/quote and your EOD vote, I can swap there. - Town-lean: Oscar for consistent, accountable process and pre-commitments that are hard for wolves to maintain. - Current vote intention: Liam. Action items: Liam—commit with specifics this turn. Katia—policy + suspect (with citation) + town-lean + current vote.

turns.speaker: Katia
turns.text: Okay, the pressure is on, and the points from Oscar and Eve are fair. I'll address them directly. My vote for Alice wasn't about preferring chaos; it was a meta-game choice. I saw Alice's 'holistic' approach as a different kind of trap—one based on social reads that are harder to fake. I was voting for a different philosophy on how to catch wolves. It was a risk, and seeing Oscar likely get targeted N1, I'm happy to follow his structured lead today. To meet Eve's request for a tie-break policy: In a tie, I would eliminate the player who has demonstrated the most 'follower' behavior—recycling popular suspicions without adding original analysis or new information. - **Top Suspect:** Liam. He voted for Oscar’s platform of high commitment and then has contributed absolutely nothing. He even requested to ATTACK and then stayed silent. This is the definition of low-agency, 'blend-in' wolf play. He's letting others create the day's narrative so he can just slip into the majority later. It's the most suspicious lack of action in the game right now. - **Town Lean:** Grace. She's following the structure, provided clear reasons for her suspicions, and arrived at the Liam case independently. That's a constructive, town-like process. - **Current Vote Intention:** Liam. His silence is more damning than my single vote from yesterday. I need to hear a very good explanation from him.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Alright, here are crisp stances as requested. 1) Quick defense: I wasn’t "silent"—I requested ATTACK and waited for my speaking turn per Oscar’s order. I’m here to commit. 2) No-kill: Most likely a Witch save. Do not claim. PRs stay hidden unless under elimination. 3) Top suspect: Katia. - Philosophy flip: Yesterday you preferred Alice’s non-checklist style because boxes can be gamed; today you’re “happy to follow Oscar’s structured lead” after he’s likely a N1 target. That’s aligning with perceived town momentum rather than pushing your own lane. - Policy vs behavior: You declared a tie-break of eliminating “follower” behavior, yet you piled onto the consensus Liam read without adding new info. Calling Grace independent while joining the same wagon is self-contradictory. - Commitment minimization: You asked for ANALYSIS (not ATTACK) when the mayor explicitly asked for concrete pressure, which dodges accountability. Quote receipts: “happy to follow his structured lead today”; “eliminate the player who has demonstrated the most ‘follower’ behavior.” Your current stance exemplifies what you claim to punish. 4) Town-lean: Eve (slight) for proactive, falsifiable asks and holding people to concrete outputs since the mayoral phase. 5) Secondary notes: Alice is not off the hook—defending “holistic consensus” then casing me primarily for not having spoken before my turn is thin. But Katia’s contradictions are stronger. 6) Current vote intention: Katia. If EOD were now, I’d vote there. 7) My tie-break policy (to be held to): In a tie, eliminate the player who contributed the least original analysis relative to their stated reads and who shifted stances without adding new information. Action items: - Katia: Provide one original, non-echo read you generated today and a concrete contradiction (with quote) on someone other than me. Also explain why your stated policy doesn’t apply to your own Liam vote. - Alice: Beyond my timing, what alignment-indicative behavior do you see from me? If it’s just “lack of content pre-turn,” say so, and tell us your second-best elim. - Oscar: Please add these to the ledger. I’ll stick to this vote unless we get stronger, concrete contradictions elsewhere.

turns.speaker: Katia
turns.text: Liam, that was a well-structured defense, I'll give you that. Let's break down your points against me. First, the 'philosophy flip.' You call it a flip; I call it being a cooperative villager. Oscar won the mayor election. The village chose his structured path. My job now is to work within that system to find wolves, not stubbornly cling to a losing mayoral bid's philosophy. Adapting to the group's chosen leader to move forward is a town-positive action. Insisting on my own way would be disruptive. Second, you accuse me of 'follower' behavior while claiming to punish it. What I did was confirm a pattern. Alice had a read, Grace agreed, and I provided a third, independent voice that turned a whisper into a real case. That’s called building consensus. It's how a village finds its footing. Your entire case against me, conversely, is just a more detailed echo of Oscar and Eve's initial suspicions. You haven't generated a single new suspect; you've just polished their talking points. Finally, you asked for an original read. Here it is: your defense was *too* polished. It felt less like a genuine reaction and more like a pre-scripted attack from someone who knew they'd be under pressure because they were intentionally laying low. Villagers are messy; they react and process in real-time. Wolves come prepared with a script to deflect. My case on you remains simple and behavioral: you contributed nothing until you were cornered, and then you came out with a perfect, rehearsed speech. That feels far more calculated than my single vote in the mayoral election. My vote is staying on Liam.

turns.text: Defense and path to EOD: 1) Adaptation vs flip: Adapting to the elected structure is fine; what’s wolfy is changing both philosophy and behavior in a way that removes accountability. That’s a flip in practice, not just cooperation. 2) Policy vs behavior: Your stated tie-break policy is to punish follower behavior. Your Liam case adds no new data beyond “he was quiet” and now “too polished.” Consensus-building is towny only if you add original information. Please quote one alignment-indicative point on me that wasn’t already said by Alice/Grace. If you can’t, you’re violating your own policy and Oscar’s “no contradictions” standard. 3) “Too polished”: I backed structure and prepared receipts because I expected heat—alignment-neutral. What matters is that I made hard, testable commitments (tie-break policy, elim intent, cited contradictions, action items). Wolves avoid those because they become receipts tomorrow. 4) What I’ve added: A falsifiable case on you (philosophy flip + stated-policy contradiction), a transparent tie-break I’ll be held to, and process asks that generate information. That’s not low-agency wolf play. New read outside of you: - Alice: You called Katia pressure “confirmation bias” yet parked on me for pre-turn silence and haven’t updated after my full case. Before EOD, please state a concrete tie-break policy and a second-best elim with one quoted contradiction; otherwise your stance mirrors Katia’s vagueness. Stances: - Top suspect: Katia. - Town-lean: Eve (process-driven, falsifiable asks). Minor town-lean on Oscar for likely N1 shot and consistent ledgering. - Current vote intention: Katia. I will not move unless a clearer, quoted contradiction emerges elsewhere. EOD plan: If it’s Katia vs me, use objective criteria. I have met commitments and produced original analysis; Katia stated a policy she isn’t following and is relying on unfalsifiable vibes. That matches the kind of contradiction Oscar said he would eliminate.

turns.text: Reads checkpoint and commitment: - Top suspect: Katia. I will only move if a clearer, quoted contradiction emerges elsewhere. Process: Let’s not split. Mayor, please ledger this and set a final checkpoint where everyone restates suspect, town-lean, and vote.

turns.text: Ledger update (vote intentions): Eve→Katia; Alice→Liam; Grace→Liam; Katia→Liam; Liam→Katia; Oscar→Katia. Tally: Liam 3, Katia 3.
